21. Mechanism Design

Focus on direct mechanisms via the revelation principle, design the optimal auction with virtual values, then verify numerically why truth-telling is dominant in a second-price auction.

  • The Revelation Principle and Optimal Auctions — One seller, one buyer with value v∼U[0,1]v \sim U[0,1]v∼U[0,1]. The revelation principle lets us study only direct mechanisms: sell iff the report meets the reserve rrr, and the winner pays rrr. The positive region of the virtual value ψ(v)=2v−1\psi(v) = 2v - 1ψ(v)=2v−1 is exactly expected revenue R(r)=r−r2R(r) = r - r^2R(r)=r−r2, maximized at r∗=0.5r^* = 0.5r∗=0.5 with 0.250.250.25. Run the lie checker and truth always wins.
  • Second-Price Auction: Truth-Telling Is Dominant — A second-price auction against one opponent (vo∼U[0,100]v_o \sim U[0,100]vo​∼U[0,100], truthful). The expected payoff of bidding bbb is U(b;v)=(vb−b2/2)/100U(b; v) = (vb - b^2/2)/100U(b;v)=(vb−b2/2)/100, a parabola peaking at b=vb = vb=v.
